title: Uluru Uses Netskope CASB to Retire VPN and Achieve Company-Wide Zero Trust
summary: Guided by its vision to “solving labor shortages and enriching people and companies,” Uluru Co., Ltd. runs a business centered on CGS (Crowd Generated Service)* and BPO (Business Process Outsourcing). With eight sites nationwide, including subsidiaries, and a workforce built around remote work, Uluru had adopted SaaS tools department by department — but lacked real-time visibility into network traffic and was carrying the vulnerability risk of its VPN appliances. In 2021, the company laid out a grand design for its shift to zero trust. For one of its final milestones — deploying a CASB (Cloud Access Security Broker) — Uluru chose Netskope. The deciding factors were its SaaS visibility, dedicated IP service, and the overall strength of Netskope Private Access (NPA) in retiring VPN altogether. Here’s the story behind how the employee who led the project — with no prior network experience, and with support from those around him — achieved full traffic visibility and VPN retirement across the entire company. *Crowd Generated Service is Uluru’s own business model built around crowd workers.

“People can start work without even thinking about the network, and the connection is fast,” Noda continues. “There’s an assumption that tightening security almost always makes work less efficient, but this shows that it can actually improve efficiency.”


The operational workflow — from detecting alerts, through response, to reporting — has been made more efficient through documented procedures. Uluru’s zero trust initiative continues to move forward steadily, and the company plans to keep strengthening its log management and analysis infrastructure.


Noda also identifies governance for the AI era as a challenge for the next one to two years. “Right now, we can’t fully grasp what data AI is generating, or what information is being sent to LLMs,” he says. What he’s aiming for isn’t a blanket ban, but a different kind of control.


“Uluru’s strength really is its venture-company spirit,” Noda says. “We want to let people use AI freely — it’s something we’re pushing company-wide right now — while still properly protecting the parts that are risky. I’d like to build guardrails that make that balance feel natural.”


Asked to speak to someone facing the same anxiety he felt when he first joined the company, Noda offers this, “Security solutions in particular tend to come with a big budget, a big scope, and a big impact, and that size can make you want to hold back. But Netskope’s design — which has a lot in common with application development — makes it a relatively low-barrier product to adopt. My advice: don’t be afraid, and start with a small goal first,” Noda says.


Guided by its vision to solve labor shortages and enrich people and companies, Uluru continues to pursue the evolution of businesses that combine AI with human capability — including shifting its BPO business toward higher, AI-enabled value. Netskope will keep supporting the security foundation underpinning that challenge.
